beliefs: For x>0, f(x) is linear with slope about -405 per unit and offset about -154: f(x) ≈ -405*x - 154 [E1, E2]
For -1<x<0, f(x) is linear with slope about 81.5 and offset about -17.56: f(x) ≈ 81.5*x - 17.56 [E2]
For x<=-1, f(x) is linear with slope about -35.52 and offset about -16.9: f(x) ≈ -35.52*x - 16.9 [E1, E2]
At x=0 exactly, f(0) = -5401.17, a large negative spike inconsistent with the surrounding branches [E1]
There is a transition interval roughly (-1, 0) where the slope changes from the shallow negative branch to the steeper positive branch [E2]
The exact behavior at x=0 and whether the transition is a smooth curve or sharp piecewise break is still uncertain?
notes: Refit each branch from E1/E2: positive side slope -405 offset -154; negative side (x<=-1) slope -35.52 offset -16.9; added a third linear regime on (-1,0) with slope ~81.5, and kept the x=0 spike.
